chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Summer at Page's Park in Durham: dance band, and marriage in 1919
summary: After Biddle he played a summer dance band in Durham that mixed ragtime, popular waltzes and few blues; he met and married his wife there in 1919, and he dislikes today's popular music.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You mentioned earlier that you were in St. Louis for a while. Was this after you were in Biddle?

Yes, this is after -- yeah, this is after Biddle. See, now, I played -- after I left Biddle University I played in Durham, North Carolina, for the summer. That's where I met mywife. I played there and then --
What kind of band was it?
It was -- this was a ragtime band --

I don't know whether it was ragtime or whether we were playing ragtime -- we was playing everything -- ragtime and jazz and everything else, because we were playing such numbers like "Rose of Washington Square" and "Isles of my Golden Dreams," that was popular. And "I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles." That's the kind of music those people like.
Were you playing --
Very few blues -- very few blues that people would ask you to play. You'd have to play one steps and real sweet ballad songs -- they were calling for that.
This is for dancing?

Yeah, this is for dancing. And they would come up and ask you, "Would you please play "Bubbles?" That's a waltz. They liked waltzing. Believe it or not -- da-da-da-da-da- And we'd play waltzes. And, well, the people really liked music because you really would get a kick out of playing good music, you know, different from the music -- well, it's still music, I guess, it's young folks music. I don't particularly care for that because I'm just one man, though.
What are you referring to?
The music of today.
Oh, today. Uh-huh.
Yeah, popular music of today. See, I'm just one man. That's the reason I say I don't like to knock music -- other people's music, but you have your likes and
your dislikes and that's why I say, I'm just one man, you know. Everybody has their likes and dislikes, but I can't stomach that. That don't have to be on there.
Well, when you were in Durham, how long were you playing in the band then?
In Durham? Well, I played the whole summer there at Page's Park.
What year was this?
This was in the year of 19 -- somewhere around the year -- when was this now -- 1919 I believe. 1917 -- that's when it was, 19 -- I believe it was, somewhere --
So, you were about 20 years old?
1917 -- I was around about 1919 -- I was about 20, yes, 1919 I was 20.
And you got married in Durham?
I got married in Durham. I got married during -- that's right, I got married in 1919.
So that dates it right there.
That dates -- that's right. I married in 1919.
And how long did you stay in Durham, just the summer?
